# E0343: malformed spread

A spread maps a tuple whose type spreads a pack, once per element, as `[..lists.len()]`. It names exactly one such tuple, and can't stand inside another spread.

- Rule: [`variadics.type-spreads`](../../reference/07-types.md#variadics.type-spreads)
- Reported at: the pack, the spread, or the tuple named.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0343:1
fn sizes<..Ts>(lists: (..List<Ts>)) -> List<i64> { [..1] }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn sizes<..Ts>(lists: (..List<Ts>)) -> List<i64> { [..lists.len()] }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0343_malformed_spread.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0343_malformed_spread.lt):

```text
── MALFORMED SPREAD ──────────────────── E0343_malformed_spread.lt:1:44  [E0343]

A spread maps a tuple whose type spreads a pack, and this one names none:

  1 │ fn sizes<..Ts>(xs: (..Ts)) -> List<i64> { [..1] }
    │                                            ^^^

A spread maps a tuple whose type spreads a pack, once per element, as
`[..lists.len()]`. It names exactly one such tuple, and can't stand inside
another spread.
```
